reproduction_notes: Baseline native libraries and driver were built by scripts/oop-id-slice-test.sh. That baseline script is expected to fail the unchanged custom-lookup tail assertion.

Preparation files use this checkout absolute path; adjust root for another checkout. Copy Id src first then Execution src for the shared crate. Exact source patches apply to that merged baseline and are authoritative over preparation recipes.
Build each standalone Cargo.toml with mise exec -- cargo build --offline --release --lib --manifest-path PATH --target-dir TARGET. Shared core uses its recorded build.rs for @rpath install name.

Build public C views with clang -dynamiclib -O2 -Itests/fixtures/oop-id-v2 FILE -L PREFIX/release -lbirnam_callable_core -Wl,-rpath,@loader_path -Wl,-install_name,@rpath/LIBRARY -o PREFIX/release/LIBRARY. Copy wrappers into each prefix; do not symlink wrappers across prefixes.

Build seam_fixture.c as a dylib using the same fixture include path. Compile driver/oop_slice.rs using edition 2024 and baseline release/deps rlibs for birnam_abi, birnam_artifact_codec, birnam_codegen, birnam_siphon, libloading.
run.py PREFIX LABEL executes all eight modes. run_extra.py PREFIX LABEL 250000 executes the callback and million-transition probes plus the original source gate.

For unit tests the copied fixture paths resolve via .cargo-target/tests/fixtures pointing to canonical tests/fixtures. cargo test --offline --locked --lib against shared-direct-source passes 43 tests.

The mixed-prefix uses original Id with candidate Execution/core. mismatch-driver expects refusal and verifies original Id remains usable. Initial mixed-owner-rejected report is the unmodified caller treating expected refusal as a failed load, not a memory fault.
Timing and concurrent process receipts precede initialization pairing guard; final-results, final-million, unit-direct-final and mismatch-check cover the guarded final build.
Only macOS ARM64 was exercised. No production install, relocation/cross-platform qualification, full worker/suspension/control qualification, or completion push.
